en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for having a nearly perfect cone shape.
The Philippine eagle, found in Mindanao, is one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan flows directly into the sea and is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a freshwater lake located inside the massive Taal Caldera, which also contains Volcano Island.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest peak in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley.
Luzon is the largest and most populous island in the Philippine archipelago, located in the northern part of the country.
The Philippine tarsier, native to Bohol, is one of the smallest primates in the world and has enormous eyes.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous people over 2,000 years ago.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected marine sanctuary known for its rich coral biodiversity.
Baguio City, located in the Cordillera Administrative Region, has a cooler climate than most Philippine cities due to its high elevation.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
